The '''Rose–Vinet equation of state''' is a set of equations used to describe the [[equation of state]] of solid objects. It is a modification of the [[Birch–Murnaghan equation of state]].<ref>{{cite journal|author1=Pascal Vinet |author2=John R. Smith |author3=John Ferrante |author4=James H. Rose  | title=Temperature effects on the universal equation of state of solids | journal=Physical Review B | volume=35|issue = 4| pages=1945–1953 |year=1987 | doi=10.1103/physrevb.35.1945| pmid=9941621 | bibcode=1987PhRvB..35.1945V |hdl=2060/19860019304| s2cid=24238001 | hdl-access=free}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sklogwiki.org/SklogWiki/index.php?title=Rose-Vinet_(Universal)_equation_of_state | website=SklogWiki | title=Rose-Vinet (Universal) equation of state}}</ref>
The initial paper discusses how the equation only depends on four inputs: the isothermal [[bulk modulus]] <math>B_0</math>, the derivative of bulk modulus with respect to pressure <math>B_0'</math>, the volume <math>V_0</math>, and the thermal expansion; all evaluated at zero pressure (<math>P=0</math>) and at a single (reference) temperature. The same equation holds for all classes of solids and a wide range of temperatures.

Let the cube root of the specific volume be

:<math>\eta=\left({\frac{V}{V_0}}\right)^{\frac{1}{3}}</math>

then the equation of state is:

:<math>P=3B_0\left(\frac{1-\eta}{\eta^2}\right)e^{\frac{3}{2}(B_0'-1)(1-\eta)}</math>

A similar equation was published by Stacey et al. in 1981.<ref>{{cite journal | author=F. D. Stacey | author2= B. J. Brennan | author3=R. D. Irvine | title=Finite strain theories and comparisons with seismological data | journal= Surveys in Geophysics | number=4 | pages=189–232 | year=1981 | doi=10.1007/BF01449185 | volume=4| bibcode= 1981GeoSu...4..189S | s2cid= 129899060 }}</ref>
